surfaces.part: cedar canopy crown mass (full 48x48 tile of overlapping conical crowns)

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 48x48 tile of dark and light green foliage clusters (conical cedar crowns with highlight flecks and dark gaps). The width profile is 48 for every row, so there is no silhouette, no ellipse, no front-edge line, and no eave shadow. There is also no distinct front face or standing body with a south face. It is a flat overlay texture, not a standing object, so neither a top plus front structure nor a front elevation applies. Reads as other.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single 16x16-ish tile of cedar crown heads, a repeating pattern of small conifer silhouettes in about 4 dark-to-mid greens on a dark green ground. Its measured facts are 11 colours per tile and 11 distinct colours in total. The references have about 108 colours per tile and 427-567 distinct colours, so it sits about 10x lower. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are tinted rather than neutral, so the shading reads as dark green rather than black sticker lines. That is a point in its favour. The texture is mostly the repeated cone shapes with little per-clump highlighting, and the ramp is shallow: roughly 4 steps against the 5-6 seen on the references' leaf clumps. As a tile overlay it is naturally simpler than a full tree, and its sparse crown heads are cleanly drawn. Still, with such a big gap in colours per tile and distinct colours and only a thin ramp, a careful artist would see it as flatter and less rich than the Beodeul references.
